verdict.rationale: Meilisearch documents a native MCP server at the POST /mcp route. Through it, MCP clients can search indexes, create indexes, add documents, and configure settings such as ranking rules, searchable attributes, and faceting. The evidence never shows search analytics being exposed through the MCP or tool-calling surface; analytics is documented only as a separate engine feature. There is also no independent or hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: analytics operations exposed via MCP/tool-calling, independent hands-on verification of the MCP server, detailed tool-level documentation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, agents can use my search indexes as a tool — an MCP server or tool-calling surface exposes query, analytics, and index operations

citations.quote: Meilisearch ships a native MCP server at the POST /mcp route so any MCP-compatible client can search your indexes directly.
Once configured, you can create indexes, add documents, configure settings, and perform searches using natural language prompts.
Update ranking rules, searchable attributes, and faceting through natural-language prompts.
